title: The Clearing for the Crane
beat: Prepared logs wait beside the stationary timber tractor.
staging: Samefallenroot atbackgroundleft, removedcentraltrunk nowshortlogs onbank; emptycab/cleararea.
alt: The empty tractor and logging trailer parked beside prepared oak logs near the stream.

references.role: Windfallen oak clearing, stream and root ball geography.

prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Make a clean machinery-and-landscape plate for the next stage at reference 1's fallen-oak clearing. The fallen trunk has now been prepared into four short bark-covered logs laid neatly on firm ground on the LEFT bank, away from the water. Keep the uprooted root mass behind them to show where the wood came from. Place reference 2's red tractor on the dry access track beside these logs, pointing LEFT; its empty logging trailer extends toward the RIGHT. The same yellow articulated log crane is mounted between cab and trailer and partly raised, its empty grapple hovering over the ground logs. The tractor is parked, wheels still, cab empty. Camera 1 metre high, wide side three-quarter view from across the clear working patch, framing the complete machine and logs with the stream along the lower-right edge. Living trees remain untouched. Detailed fern-rich dimensional woodland children's-book style, soft late-morning sunlight, textured highlights. No animals, people, lettering or panels. Landscape1536x1024.
review: Accepted working location: empty cab/trailer and intact living trees, cut logs beside original root ball, stream along near-right. Crane base behind cab and open grapple readable. Five log ends appear instead of requested four; prose intentionally does not specify count. This is a new staging view, not exact metric reconstruction.
